title: Optimisers: SGD, momentum, Adam, and the learning rate above all

videos.script: Training a network means taking steps downhill. This lesson is about how to take them. {{batch}} Nobody computes the exact gradient on a whole data set. A batch of thirty-two images gives an estimate, noisy but pointing roughly the right way. {{valley}} The loss is rarely a round bowl. Picture a long, narrow valley. Plain gradient descent bounces from wall to wall and crawls along the floor. {{momentum}} Momentum keeps a velocity, so the steps that agree add up. After forty steps it is fifteen times closer to the bottom. {{adam}} Adam goes further and gives every parameter a step size of its own. A gradient of one hundred and a gradient of a hundredth take the same step. {{code}} Then all three go into one small module, with the training loop that every lesson up to the eighth will use. {{sweep}} And then the most useful result of the lesson. Thirty runs, ten learning rates for each optimiser. The rate moves accuracy by eighty-seven points. The optimiser moves it by about one. {{schedule}} Last, the rate does not have to stay fixed. A schedule lowers it as training goes, and rescues a rate that was too high. {{end}}
